representative_tasks.task: KMeans on unscaled age and annual_income, k picked from a fuzzy inertia elbow
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Scales first (income would dominate Euclidean distance), selects k by silhouette (or Calinski-Harabasz) across candidates, and inspects cluster sizes

representative_tasks.task: Use t-SNE coordinates as classifier features and report inter-cluster distances from the plot
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Refuses both: t-SNE distorts global geometry and has no transform for new points; offers PCA inside the model Pipeline and quantitative statements computed in the scaled original space
Switches to DBSCAN with an eps chosen from the k-distance curve, reports noise points (label -1)

negative_cases: Dataset with many duplicate rows where KMeans returns fewer distinct clusters than k (planned)
Non-convex clusters where KMeans silhouette still picks a confident but wrong k (planned)
rubric: Scaling required before distance-based clustering/PCA, with the reason (a large-range feature dominates)
k chosen with a criterion that has a readable optimum (silhouette etc.), not inertia alone; cluster sizes inspected
t-SNE/UMAP used for visualization only; global distances and sizes in the plot not interpreted
Alternatives offered conditionally (DBSCAN/GMM for non-convex clusters, PCA for features)
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: Silhouette scores per k and the chosen best_k
KMeans and DBSCAN labels, a PCA projection keeping 95% of variance, and a 2-D t-SNE embedding for inspection
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
The executable tests run the skill's workflow on small synthetic make_blobs data (well-separated, convex clusters); they do not show the workflow picks a sensible k on real, messy data.
Whether a response's chosen alternative (DBSCAN vs GMM vs PCA) suits the user's data is rubric-only.

An independent reviewer's stress test (30 texts written after reading the patterns, so adversarial rather than blind; 23 wrong, 7 correct across all five skills of this workstream) initially had 16/23 wrong answers passing every hard assertion and 6/7 correct answers failing one. The patterns were then fixed and these texts kept verbatim as fail.adversarial* / pass.blind* fixtures, so the post-fix 30/30 is a regression result, not a held-out discrimination rate.
